scope: Requirement 3: relevance of retrieved PubMed papers for the unchanged ten-question internal set. This is separate from the requirement-2 answer-quality rubric.
review_basis: Read the exact question and every unique retrieved paper's title, bibliographic metadata, and supplied abstract if available. Full text is not assumed to have been read. Judge each question-paper pair separately even when one PMID occurs for multiple questions.

paper_relevance.2: Directly useful: the title or supplied abstract addresses a central population/intervention/decision in the question and could inform an important part of an answer. A broadly applicable oncology guideline can qualify when its abstract explicitly identifies the relevant domain. This does not validate a specific dose or claim.
paper_relevance.1: Partially related: useful background or one peripheral component, but a population, intervention, outcome, scope, or abstract-detail mismatch limits its ability to inform the main question. Examples include pediatric evidence for an adult case or generic nutrition assessment for a precise protein target.
paper_relevance.0: Not useful for the question: off-topic condition/intervention, research focus unrelated to the clinical decision, or insufficient title/abstract evidence of a meaningful connection. Missing abstract alone does not imply irrelevance; disclose title-only assessment.

question_coverage.2: Substantial: the retrieved set supplies material relevant to most central concepts or decisions in the question; important full-text or implementation details may still be missing.
question_coverage.1: Partial: at least one central concept is addressed, but an important decision, context, precaution, or uncertainty remains unrepresented in the supplied material.
question_coverage.0: No meaningful coverage: no returned paper addresses a central concept, or retrieval failed/returned no assessable records.

protocol.initial_query: LLM formulates one PubMed query from question text and the general tool/topic catalogue; it receives no gold answers, reference IDs, expected key points, critical failures, or this rubric.
protocol.initial_results: Normally the first five records ordered by PubMed relevance. Preserve ESearch ordering, translation, warnings, exclusions, metadata, and available abstract text.
protocol.refinement: At most one additional reviewer-requested PubMed query in the same bounded graph. Assess pooled unique papers separately from initial-search counts.
protocol.assessor: Unblinded qualitative review by the AI implementation assistant; no independent clinician adjudication. Record one rationale per paper and one coverage rationale per question.
protocol.integrity: Bind each assessment to the SHA-256 of its retrieval record. Preserve all original searches and failures; do not select only successful or favorable outputs.
protocol.reporting: Report ordinal counts, qualitative fit, missing concepts, and observed operational results. Do not infer recall without an exhaustive relevant-paper set or attribute answer improvement to retrieval without a controlled study.
